name: block-hook-bypass-in-files
description: Friction, not a security boundary: flags lines added to hook launchers and scripts that switch git hooks off -- the hook-skip option on a git commit/push/merge/am/rebase/pull, core.hooksPath set by git config or GIT_CONFIG_*, the husky, lefthook and pre-commit off-switch variables, a pre-commit, lefthook or husky (v8 and older) uninstall -- in .husky/, .githooks/, lefthook, package.json, Makefile, justfile, .envrc, *.sh. Blocks. Misses: split lines, -n. [Session-enforced via PreToolUse and Stop hooks; needs git and a Python 3.11+. PreToolUse judges the file a tool call would write; Stop re-reads what the turn actually left on disk, so a file written through a shell heredoc is judged too. With no working Python the hook exits 2; without git, fail-open clients allow silently. A gate that cannot reach a decision refuses rather than allowing one it never judged. Enforcement at every commit and in CI still needs chock installed in the repo. Codex requires a one-time trust review per hook -- the plugin is ADVISORY until you approve its hook, and a plugin update voids that trust until re-approved.]
